name: create-realm
description: Records a second realm, with you as its admin.

name: put-account
description: Adds an account, which lands in the realm the part names.

name: put-account-keeps-the-owner
description: Putting an account that exists again leaves its owner and realm alone.

name: put-account-in-another-realm
description: An account created inside a realm of its own.

name: merge-accounts
description: Rebooks every posting into another account and removes the emptied one.

name: delete-account
description: Removes an account no posting mentions.

name: set-account-rights
description: Names a second member as a poster on an account.

name: set-account-rights-to-nobody
description: An empty list: the boundary case of a list field.

name: set-account-owner
description: Hands an account to somebody else.

name: put-label
description: Adds a label.

name: put-label-with-empty-strings
description: Empty strings, which encode as a zero length.

name: delete-label
description: Removes a label, and strips it from the transaction carrying it.

name: put-party
description: Adds a counterparty.

name: put-group
description: Saves a named set of people to split costs with.

name: delete-group
description: Removes a group, leaving the people alone.

name: put-trip
description: A trip spanning the two ends of what a date can hold.

name: delete-trip
description: Removes a trip by name.

name: put-rule
description: A rule whose filter nests, so the recursive encoding is exercised.

name: put-rule-with-empty-lists
description: Empty strings, an empty list and a negative priority.

name: delete-rule
description: Removes a rule by name.

name: add-member
description: Records another identity, and the party their spending lands on.

name: member-introduces-themselves
description: Somebody who joined through an invite writes their own member record, and the party that comes with it.

name: remove-member
description: Removes an identity that is not the ledger's own.

name: grant
description: Lets a member into a realm, with the purse they hold a balance in.

name: bridge-owner-is-the-members-party
description: The purse a grant opens belongs to the member it is for, whatever the operation says.

name: member-self-grants-as-viewer
description: A joiner attests the viewer grant the sequencer already holds for them.

name: set-role
description: Changes what a member may do in a realm.

name: revoke
description: Puts a member out, and bumps the realm's key generation.

name: rotate-realm-key
description: Bumps a realm's key generation on its own.

name: record-import-batch
description: Records one run of an importer over one file.

name: refuses-a-snapshot-in-a-part
description: A snapshot is where a log starts, not something a part may say — not even on a ledger nothing has happened in. Where a log starts is a fact about the reader's position in the order, and a reader holding one key generation folds nothing written under any other, so a state that looks untouched part way along is not a beginning.

name: put-transaction
description: Writes a balanced transaction.

name: put-transaction-imported
description: A transaction off a bank line, which spends its import fingerprint.

name: delete-transaction
description: Removes a transaction.

name: split-three-ways
description: Ten thousand between three people: the remainder goes out a cent at a time.

name: split-one-cent-two-ways
description: One cent between two people: one of them gets nothing.

name: split-without-keeping-a-share
description: The whole amount goes to the two of them.

name: merge-transactions
description: Combines a purchase with the fee the bank posted beside it.

name: unmerge-transaction
description: Splits the merged transaction back into what it was built from.

name: replace-transaction
description: Divides a payment into parts that take exactly the money the original took.

name: split-a-refund-three-ways
description: A hundred cents back, between three: Euclidean division makes that -34, -33, -33.

name: divide-by-items
description: Two of the six units a line covers go to her; the rest stays behind.

name: claim-a-cost
description: Says a cost of a budget was yours to bear, rather than everybody's.

name: release-a-cost
description: And gives it back.

name: divide-a-part-again
description: A remainder is divided by the lines it was left with, numbered from one.

name: raise-claim
description: A claim: a dated movement that is expected and has not happened.

name: resolve-claim-in-full
description: The money arrived in full, so the claim is settled and stamped.

name: resolve-claim-in-part
description: Two thousand of five: the part that was met becomes a record of its own.

name: void-claim
description: Retires a claim that will never be performed.

name: void-claim-with-a-write-off
description: The same, with the loss booked where it belongs.

name: pay-claim
description: The member who is owed records the payment: the payment and the settlement in one.

name: pay-claim-by-an-admin
description: An admin of the realm the two purses sit in may record it too.

name: refuses-paying-your-own-debt
description: The member who owes a claim cannot write the receipt for it themselves.

name: refuses-paying-a-settled-claim
description: A claim that has already been met cannot be paid again.

name: refuses-a-claim-with-three-legs
description: A claim is exactly two legs: one account owes and one is owed.

name: open-budget
description: Opens a budget and the equity account that holds it.

name: set-participants
description: Names who a budget is divided among.

name: set-participants-to-nobody
description: An empty list of participants.

name: contribute
description: Records a cost somebody paid for directly into a budget.

name: allocate-equally
description: Divides sixteen thousand between two people and raises the claim.

name: allocate-by-weight
description: The same money, in a two-to-one split.

name: allocate-tops-up-a-late-cost
description: A receipt that turned up afterwards is divided on its own, topping each person up.

name: allocate-through-a-hub
description: Three people, squared up through one of them instead of by the shortest plan.

name: settle-through-a-hub
description: Re-planning through a hub revises one claim, raises another and withdraws a third.

name: close-budget
description: Divides what is left and closes the budget.

name: allocate-a-negative-cost
description: A discount, divided three ways: a negative amount, and the remainder goes the other way.

name: reopen-budget
description: Reopens it; every division already made stands.

name: delete-budget
description: Removes a budget, leaving the transactions it touched alone.

name: issue-invoice
description: Numbers an invoice gaplessly and gives it a structured reference.

name: issue-invoice-for-an-unknown-payer
description: A payer nobody knows yet is recorded as a party by the same operation.

name: set-invoice-status
description: Moves an invoice to a new status.

name: settle-invoice
description: Marks it paid, and records which transaction settled it.

name: delete-invoice
description: Deletes a draft, winding the year's counter back.

name: register-blob
description: Records a stored file's metadata.

name: re-register-blob-with-a-wrap
description: A file the ledger already knows, re-sealed under another realm: the ciphertext's hash and the wrapped key are taken, and nothing else about it is.

name: attach
description: Links a receipt to a transaction.

name: detach
description: Unlinks it again.

name: record-extraction
description: Stores what was read off a receipt.

name: set-receipt-lines
description: Replaces the lines printed on it, short of the total.

name: forget-blob
description: Forgets a stored file nothing points at.

name: refuses-an-unbalanced-transaction
description: A transaction whose postings do not sum to zero.

name: refuses-a-closed-account
description: A posting into an account that is closed.

name: refuses-a-member-without-rights
description: A second member, who administers nothing and was named on nothing.

name: refuses-a-missing-transaction
description: An operation naming something that is not there.

name: refuses-a-duplicate-fingerprint
description: A bank line that has already been imported.

name: refuses-a-cost-on-a-closed-budget
description: A closed budget takes no more costs.

name: refuses-too-few-fresh-ids
description: Unmerging into fewer ids than there are origins.

name: refuses-a-settled-claim
description: A claim that has already been met asks for nothing.

name: refuses-deleting-a-sent-invoice
description: A number somebody has seen is voided, not deleted.

name: refuses-an-account-merged-into-itself
description: A merge that would empty and fill one account.

name: refuses-an-empty-group
description: A group needs at least one member.

name: refuses-a-grant-by-a-non-admin
description: Only an admin of a realm may let somebody in.

name: refuses-a-self-grant-as-admin
description: What a member may attest about themselves is a view; an admin role is a takeover.

name: refuses-a-self-grant-for-somebody-else
description: A member may speak for themselves. Letting a third person in is still an admin's decision.

name: refuses-a-grant-that-moves-an-account
description: A grant hands out a purse; it never moves an account that is already elsewhere.

name: participant-posts-to-an-open-budget
description: Anybody in the realm may put a cost into a budget of it while the budget is open.

name: refuses-posting-to-a-closed-budget-account
description: A closed budget is a decided one, so the right to put costs into it ends with it.

name: refuses-a-division-that-invents-money
description: Parts that take less out of the funding account than the original did.

name: mixed-parts-second-refused
description: A valid part beside an invalid one, which is skipped.

name: mixed-parts-first-refused
description: The invalid part first: its neighbour still applies.

name: mixed-parts-middle-refused
description: Three parts, and the one in the middle is refused.

name: refuses-a-realm-that-exists
description: A realm id that is already spoken for.

name: refuses-deleting-an-account-with-postings
description: An account something still lands in.

name: refuses-rights-on-a-missing-account
description: Rights named on an account that is not there.

name: refuses-handing-over-a-missing-account
description: The same, for an account's owner.

name: refuses-a-missing-rule
description: A rule named by neither id nor name.

name: refuses-a-split-with-nobody-to-split-with
description: A split naming no targets.

name: refuses-a-merge-of-one
description: Merging needs at least two transactions.

name: refuses-a-division-with-no-groups
description: Dividing by lines that were never named.

name: refuses-taking-a-cost-twice
description: The same person, the same cost, a second time.

name: refuses-taking-what-is-not-a-cost-of-the-budget
description: A transaction with no leg in the budget's account.

name: refuses-giving-back-what-nobody-took
description: A cost no claim was made on.

name: refuses-giving-back-somebody-elses-cost
description: A member of the realm who is not an admin, undoing another's claim.

name: refuses-a-line-that-went-to-a-sibling
description: A part holds the two lines it was left with, and a third number is not one of them.

name: refuses-a-claim-that-has-happened
description: A claim is a transaction that has not happened.

name: refuses-voiding-a-transaction
description: A posted transaction is not a claim to withdraw.

name: refuses-a-budget-opened-by-a-non-admin
description: Only an admin of a realm may open a budget in it.

name: refuses-participants-on-a-missing-budget
description: A budget nobody opened.

name: refuses-a-share-in-an-account-of-yours
description: A share of hers may not land in an account of yours.

name: refuses-settling-a-budget-still-holding-money
description: There would be a residue belonging to nobody.

name: refuses-closing-a-closed-budget
description: Closing one that is already closed.

name: refuses-reopening-an-open-budget
description: Reopening one that was never closed.

name: refuses-deleting-a-missing-budget
description: A budget nobody opened.

name: refuses-an-invoice-id-that-exists
description: An invoice id that is already spoken for.

name: refuses-a-status-on-a-missing-invoice
description: An invoice that was never raised.

name: refuses-settling-an-invoice-with-a-missing-transaction
description: The entry that is said to have paid it is not there.

name: refuses-attaching-a-missing-receipt
description: A content hash nothing is stored under.

name: refuses-detaching-from-a-missing-transaction
description: A transaction that is not there.

name: refuses-an-extraction-of-a-missing-receipt
description: Nothing is stored under that hash.

name: refuses-lines-past-the-total
description: Lines may fall short of what a receipt says it came to, and never overrun it.

name: refuses-forgetting-a-missing-receipt
description: Nothing is stored under that hash.

name: refuses-a-member-added-by-a-non-admin
description: A member introduces themselves; writing somebody else in is an admin's decision.

name: refuses-removing-yourself
description: The member this ledger belongs to cannot be removed.

name: refuses-a-revoke-by-a-non-admin
description: Only an admin of a realm may put somebody out.

name: refuses-a-role-for-somebody-outside-the-realm
description: A role can only be changed for somebody who holds one.

name: refuses-rotating-a-missing-realm
description: A realm nobody created, and so nobody administers.

name: refuses-an-author-outside-the-realm
description: Every operation asks first whether its author is in the realm the part names.

name: refuses-a-realm-member-without-post-rights
description: Being in the realm is not being able to write in it.

name: refuses-a-snapshot-once-anything-has-happened
description: A snapshot replaces the state, so it is the first thing a log says or it is a takeover.

name: refuses-a-snapshot-by-an-admin-of-the-realm
description: Not even an admin: `applyOp` refuses every snapshot, wherever it appears and whoever wrote it, and `replay` reads the genesis off the first event of the log instead.

name: refuses-a-transaction-with-no-postings
description: An empty posting list balances vacuously, which made it a way to rewrite any transaction's metadata — including voiding it.

name: refuses-a-transaction-that-is-not-posted
description: A transaction is written as something that happened; the other states belong to claims.

name: refuses-too-many-postings
description: A list an author chose the length of is bounded.

name: refuses-too-many-participants
description: The same, for the people a budget is divided among.

name: refuses-a-weight-out-of-range
description: A share's weight is a small number.

name: refuses-a-line-quantity-nobody-printed
description: A receipt line covering a thousand million units is how one small event made every reader allocate a list of that length.

name: refuses-an-identifier-that-is-too-long
description: An id is a name, not a document.

name: refuses-a-year-out-of-range
description: A date's year is the one part of a date no type bounds, and a ledger keeping books a million years hence is a number somebody sent, not a date.

name: refuses-an-exponent-out-of-range
description: A commodity's scale is ten to the power of its exponent, so an exponent an author chose is a bignum an author chose the length of.

name: refuses-a-realm-with-somebody-else-inside-it
description: A realm is created with its author as its only admin; the membership list is not the author's to choose.

name: refuses-a-realm-at-a-rotated-generation
description: A new realm starts at generation 0: a history that begins after a revoke is a lie.

name: refuses-an-account-written-by-a-viewer
description: Whoever may write an account into a realm decides who posts to everything in it.

name: refuses-rewriting-an-account-of-another-realm
description: An account is rewritten from the realm it sits in, and no other.

name: refuses-a-merge-by-a-viewer
description: A merge empties the account it names, so it asks about that one too.

name: refuses-an-account-deleted-by-a-viewer
description: Removing an account is an admin's.

name: refuses-rights-set-by-a-viewer
description: So is saying who may post where.

name: refuses-an-account-handed-over-by-a-viewer
description: And so is handing one to somebody.

name: refuses-a-label-written-by-a-viewer
description: A label is shared vocabulary, and the first one of a name used to decide which claims a budget could see.

name: refuses-a-label-deleted-by-a-viewer
description: Deleting a label strips it from every transaction carrying it.

name: refuses-a-party-rewritten-by-a-viewer
description: A party record is what a settlement is addressed to.

name: refuses-a-group-written-by-a-viewer
description: A saved set of people is the realm's.

name: refuses-a-trip-written-by-a-viewer
description: So is a trip.

name: refuses-a-rule-written-by-a-viewer
description: Rules drive what an import files where.

name: refuses-an-import-batch-by-a-viewer
description: And so is the record of an import.

name: reads-a-newcomers-claim-on-the-ledgers-party-as-their-own
description: A member's party is what their spending is attributed to, and the ledger's own party is whoever is reading, so a record naming it that this node did not write is read as a party of that member's own, keyed by their key.

name: refuses-a-newcomer-taking-somebody-elses-party
description: Nor anybody else's: it would put their movements in that person's standing.

name: refuses-a-grant-for-another-realm
description: The evidence a sequencer holds is a grant on the realm the part names, so that is the only realm a part can speak about.

name: refuses-rewriting-a-transaction-with-no-leg-here
description: A part with nothing of this realm's to replace has no business replacing the metadata.

name: refuses-deleting-somebody-elses-transaction
description: A transaction is retired by somebody who could have written it.

name: refuses-splitting-somebody-elses-transaction
description: The same holds of every arithmetic intent over it.

name: refuses-attaching-to-somebody-elses-transaction
description: A receipt is hung on a transaction by somebody who may post to it.

name: refuses-detaching-from-somebody-elses-transaction
description: And taken off the same way.

name: refuses-a-claim-raised-by-a-viewer
description: Asking somebody for money in the realm's name is an admin's decision.

name: refuses-voiding-a-claim-by-the-debtor
description: Withdrawing a claim is the creditor's decision; the debtor doing it is not paying.

name: refuses-voiding-a-claim-that-was-met
description: Withdrawing a settled claim took the payment out of the settlement arithmetic, so the same money was asked for twice.

name: refuses-resolving-a-claim-by-the-debtor
description: Saying money arrived is the decision of whoever would have seen it arrive.

name: refuses-paying-a-claim-into-an-account-that-holds-no-money
description: A payment into an equity leg was rewritten onto the paying account, so the claim came out met and nothing had moved.

name: refuses-participants-named-by-a-viewer
description: Who a budget is divided among is an admin's decision.

name: refuses-an-allocation-by-a-viewer
description: So is dividing what it holds.

name: refuses-a-budget-decided-from-another-realm
description: A budget belongs to one realm, and a decision about it has to be written under its key.

name: refuses-taking-money-out-of-a-budget
description: A participant's right on the pot is a right to contribute. A pot everybody may take out of is not a pot.

name: refuses-an-invoice-issued-by-a-viewer
description: Burning a number in your sequence, or winding it back, is not a viewer's to do.

name: refuses-an-invoice-status-set-by-a-viewer
description: Nor is moving one to a new status.

name: refuses-a-receipt-rewritten-by-somebody-else
description: Only the member who filed the bytes, somebody who may post what they belong to, or an admin, may say what a receipt contains.

name: refuses-an-extraction-by-somebody-else
description: The same for what was read off it.

name: refuses-re-registering-somebody-elses-file
description: Re-sealing a file is a decision about where their bytes are kept.

name: refuses-forgetting-a-receipt-by-a-viewer
description: Forgetting one is an admin's.

name: put-label-in-another-realm
description: A label is created in the realm the part names, and carries it.

name: refuses-rewriting-a-label-of-another-realm
description: Shared vocabulary belongs to the people who share it.

name: refuses-deleting-a-label-of-another-realm
description: Deleting a label strips it from the transactions carrying it, and those are not this part's to rewrite.

name: refuses-rewriting-a-party-of-another-realm
description: A party record is what a settlement is addressed to, and it belongs to the realm the person was introduced in.

name: member-revises-their-own-party-from-any-realm
description: The one entity a member owns outright: the party their own spending lands on. They may revise it from any realm they are in, and the record keeps the realm it was introduced in.

name: refuses-a-group-of-another-realm
description: A saved set of people is a realm's.

name: refuses-deleting-a-group-of-another-realm
description: And so is removing one.

name: refuses-a-trip-of-another-realm
description: So is a trip.

name: refuses-deleting-a-trip-of-another-realm
description: And removing one.

name: refuses-a-rule-of-another-realm
description: Rules drive what an import files where, so they are the realm's they were written in.

name: refuses-an-import-batch-of-another-realm
description: And so is the record of an import.

name: refuses-rewriting-a-receipt-filed-in-another-realm
description: Whoever filed a receipt keeps the right to say what it contains — in the realm they filed it in, and not from any other realm they hold a key for.

name: refuses-forgetting-a-receipt-filed-in-another-realm
description: Forgetting one is an admin's, of the realm the bytes were filed in.

name: refuses-an-invoice-touched-from-another-realm
description: An invoice record carries the realm it was issued in, and the counter is keyed by realm — so deleting a draft from anywhere else wound back a sequence that had never issued it: the issuing realm kept the burnt number, and the next invoice in the other realm duplicated one already sent. Setting the status and recording a settlement go through the same door.

name: invoice-payer-resolved-in-this-realm
description: The payer is looked up by name inside the part's realm. The lookup used to be the first party of that name in id order across every realm a reader could open, and a member may set the name of their own party to anything from any realm they are in — so an invoice to a name you both know was addressed to whichever record sorted first.

name: refuses-a-settlement-account-from-another-realm
description: The account a person settles through is looked for in the budget's own realm. An account of theirs in another realm is refused as a candidate here, rather than chosen and then refused by the posting rules — which is what used to happen, and it stopped every settlement of the budget until somebody closed or renamed an account in a realm that had nothing to do with it.

name: invoice-numbering-is-per-realm
description: The year's counter is keyed by realm. One sequence for the whole ledger meant an admin of any realm a reader could open moved the ledger owner's invoice numbering.

name: self-grant-makes-the-canonical-bridge
description: A member attesting their own viewer grant opens one purse: named after them, of the kind money is held in, with nobody else on it and mirroring nothing. Everything else the operation carries is ignored, because the door is open to any member about themselves and it used to write the name, the kind and the posters verbatim.

name: refuses-a-self-grant-onto-a-name-that-exists
description: Nothing is adopted by the attest door either: a joiner taking over an account that is already there is the same hole read backwards.

name: refuses-a-self-grant-onto-an-id-that-exists
description: Nor by id.

name: refuses-a-budget-held-in-somebody-s-purse
description: A viewer who self-granted a purse called `Budget.Hut` before the budget was opened had the pot adopted as their own bridge, which they may post to in either direction.

name: open-budget-adopts-a-plain-equity-account
description: An account of the budget's name that is a pot and nobody's purse is adopted, which is what makes opening a budget over one that is already there say nothing new.

name: allocate-to-a-participant-s-bridge
description: A share may land in the purse a member holds in this realm: a bridge belongs to the member it is for, and their spending lands on their party, so both readings of "an account of theirs" are allowed and nothing else is.

name: receiver-resolves-their-own-claim
description: The member whose purse was owed says the money arrived, without post rights on the debtor's purse. The rights table always granted this and the arithmetic never allowed it: settling writes the claim back, and the claim's paying leg is the debtor's.

name: refuses-overwriting-a-stored-claim
description: A claim is met or withdrawn, never overwritten. Rewriting one as a posted transaction took it out of the settlement arithmetic and put its amounts into every balance, without going through either claim verb.

name: refuses-overwriting-a-settled-claim
description: The same door reached a claim that had already been met, and so booked money that had already moved a second time.

name: refuses-a-split-that-computes-too-many-postings
description: `checkBounds` refuses a transaction of more than two hundred legs that an author *sends*; this is one an intent computed, which nothing used to bound at all.

name: boundary-leb128-127
description: An amount of 127 minor units: the last one-byte LEB128.

name: boundary-leb128-128
description: An amount of 128: the first two-byte LEB128.

name: boundary-leb128-16383
description: An amount of 16383: the last two-byte LEB128.

name: boundary-leb128-16384
description: An amount of 16384 and an event based on 16384: the first three-byte LEB128.

name: boundary-negative-amounts
description: A refund: the expense leg is the negative one.

name: boundary-empty-strings
description: An empty narration and an empty payee.

name: boundary-empty-event
description: An event with no parts at all, which changes nothing.

name: boundary-date-2000-01-01
description: A transaction on the earliest date the vectors use.

name: boundary-date-2099-12-31
description: A transaction on the latest date the vectors use.
